steps.domain_action: Initialize the domain with an empty set of integers before any LCM computation.
Recognize the intrinsic property that consecutive integers n and n-1 are coprime.
Diverge the analysis into two parallel evaluation paths: the lower bound and the upper comparison.
Advance the T-arm to compute the quadratic lower bound n(n-1) derived from the coprime product.
Affirm that n(n-1) divides the LCM, establishing the constructive truth of the lower bound.
Chain the divisibility of n and n-1 to the product n(n-1) within the T-arm.
Descend the F-arm to evaluate the logarithmic comparison term n*log(n+1).
Refute the dominance of the logarithmic term by showing log(n+1) < n-1 for n >= 3.
Chain the exponential inequality e^(n-1) > n+1 to the logarithmic bound in the F-arm.
Rejoin the T-arm (quadratic lower) and F-arm (logarithmic upper) to resolve the strict inequality.
Hold the paradice state where the exclusion of n=1,2 and inclusion of n>=3 coexist as a density-one set.
Permanently record the formal verification of the inequality in the Lean proof assistant.
Anchor the system at the boundary n=3, defining the closed region where the theorem holds.
Self-reference the completed theorem as a stable object within the mathematical landscape.
